request.spec:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.

You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Grace days are in, and `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 tests in the spec, with the audit lines matching what they expect.

**What it does**
- **The setting:** grace days are a whole number, and blank means off. They aren't dated, so they're stored in a new column, `V37__grace_days.sql`. Saving writes `SETTING_CHANGED key=grace-days value=<days>`. The Settings panel has a `setting-grace-days` input and a `setting-grace-days-current` display.
- **Auto close:** when the sheet's today changes, a new step (`period/AutoClosePeriods.java`) runs after the new date is saved and before the rollup lines. It closes every open period whose to-date plus the grace days is before the new today, in order of to-date. Each one writes `PERIOD_CLOSED ... total=<t> auto=yes`. It does nothing when grace days are blank.
- **Same close logic for both:** I moved the closing work out of `ClosePeriod` into a shared `period/PeriodCloser.java`, so the automatic close and the close by hand run identical code. `ClosePeriod` keeps its role check and its "already closed" refusal.
- **Front end:** after a today change, the screen now re-reads the periods list too, so an auto-closed period shows `period-closed` = `yes` straight away.

**Decision for you:** the auto close does not check whether the person changing today has the "close" permission. I read "exactly as a close by hand would" as being about how the totals are worked out, not about who is allowed. The tests don't cover this either way. If you want a today change by someone who can't close periods to skip the auto close, it's a one-line check in `AutoClosePeriods`.
